subject: conditional diffusion model
statement: The paper proposes a conditional diffusion model that applies hard filtering, soft weighting, or projection-based repair to improve structural validity of trajectories in dynamic graph-structured systems.

subject: compact graph regime
statement: The paper reports invalid probability mass of 0.002996 in the compact graph regime, indicating an almost entirely admissible trajectory manifold.

subject: medium-complexity regime
statement: The paper reports invalid mass increases to 0.155929 in the medium-complexity dependency graph regime.

subject: hard filtering
statement: The paper shows hard filtering removes all invalid retained trajectories while preserving 84.4% of generated samples.

subject: semantic-aware task clustering
statement: The paper proposes semantic-aware task clustering for cooperative multi-task semantic communication using hierarchical density-based spatial clustering and intra-cluster end-to-end training.

subject: multi-tasking framework
statement: Simulation results demonstrate the proposed framework yields accuracy gains compared to unclustered multi-tasking and individual training baselines.

subject: Agent-Guided Concept Discovery
statement: The paper proposes Agent-Guided Concept Discovery that learns human-understandable concepts from REIMS data without requiring predefined concept labels.

subject: reasoning agent refinement
statement: During training, a reasoning agent refines semantic descriptions of learned concepts and adaptively adjusts their weight based on diagnostic relevance.

subject: biochemical knowledge grounding
statement: The paper grounds learned concepts using biochemical knowledge graph to ensure consistency with known metabolic relationships.

subject: Skin and Breast Cancer datasets
statement: The paper shows across Skin and Breast Cancer datasets the model improves balanced accuracy and sensitivity over baseline and demonstrates fewer false positives in intraoperative cases.

subject: FGDSE ensemble framework
statement: The paper develops FGDSE, a feature-governed dynamic stacking ensemble with four feature families and two deep temporal experts for climate-resilient EV charging asset management.

subject: 25-month station evaluation
statement: On 25 months of data from 13 stations, FGDSE surpasses twelve baselines beyond the ten-day forecast horizon.

subject: 30-day performance
statement: The paper shows system sustains approximately 85% macro-recall at 30 days with AUC decay of only 3.2 points.

subject: extreme heat causal effect
statement: The paper identifies extreme heat as the sole exposure whose causal effect amplifies over time, flagging roughly 30% of posts as heat-sensitive.

subject: TriviaRoomQA benchmark
statement: The paper introduces TriviaRoomQA, a multilingual benchmark with 3,300 parallel multiple-choice questions in six European languages across 288 topics, plus 5,340 French-only questions.

subject: 30 open-weight LLMs
statement: Evaluation of 30 open-weight LLMs (7-70B parameters) shows models are strong on knowledge-intensive topics such as history, geography, and mathematics.

subject: popular culture topics
statement: The paper shows models substantially weaker on everyday popular-culture topics such as celebrities, music, movies, and news, with performance varying across languages.

subject: KroQuant PTQ method
statement: The paper proposes KroQuant, a post-training quantization method applying learned Kronecker-structured invertible transforms to 32-element activation blocks.

subject: MI350 GPU performance
statement: The paper reports KroQuant quantizer kernel runs up to 14% faster than SmoothQuant kernel on MI350 GPU.

subject: PixArt SANA FLUX models
statement: On PixArt-Σ, SANA, and FLUX.1-schnell at W4A4 (MXFP4e2), KroQuant produces outputs closer to FP reference than SVDQuant and LoRaQ while preserving image quality.

subject: TTEL algorithm
statement: The paper introduces TTEL, an inference-time algorithm that uses feedback to perform token-level error localization and truncate/branch generation to maximize prefix reuse.

subject: Qwen3-8B LiveCodeBench
statement: With Qwen3-8B on LiveCodeBench, TTEL attains pass@64 of 71.0% while generating approximately half as many tokens as independent sampling (360.4k vs 735.0k).

subject: AIME HMMT benchmarks
statement: The paper shows TTEL cleanly outperforms competing test-time baselines on AIME-2025 and HMMT-2025 across Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507.

subject: token-level detection method
statement: The paper proposes token-level method for detecting LLM-generated content in mixed-authorship documents using smoothed token scores and adaptive bandwidth selection.

subject: Lepski-type rule
statement: The paper shows method achieves favorable mean square error performance without requiring token-level labeled training data.

subject: AREX agents
statement: The paper introduces AREX, a family of Recursively Self-Improving agents that alternate between inner research loop gathering evidence and outer self-improvement loop performing constraint-wise verification.

subject: context-update tool
statement: AREX learns autonomous context-update tool compressing interaction history into compact improvement state preserving verified evidence and unresolved constraints.

subject: AREX model variants
statement: The paper instantiates AREX as dense 4B model and 122B-A10B Mixture-of-Experts model trained on verified synthetic tasks and high-quality trajectories.

subject: multi-benchmark evaluation
statement: Across BrowseComp, WideSearch, DeepSearchQA, and Humanity's Last Exam, AREX substantially outperforms comparable-scale baselines and remains competitive with substantially larger models.

subject: Thinkink tool
statement: The paper introduces Thinkink, a tool for ink-native LLM interaction where user and LLM write and draw in shared 2D canvas with ink-like visualization.

subject: semantic tree state machine
statement: Semantic tree streamlines ink interpretation and lightweight UI provides explicit control using state machine for prompt and response management.

subject: three-stage design process
statement: The paper contributes design implications through three-stage process: formative study (N=12), diagnostic study (N=6), and final study (N=10) examining ideation integration.

subject: deterministic KV-cache eviction
statement: The paper proves deterministic KV-cache eviction cannot provide consistent serving-time estimates of true attention-output error.

subject: randomized eviction
statement: Randomized eviction with Poisson-sampled tail at known inclusion probabilities restores identifiability with Hájek correction in softmax.

subject: error certificate
statement: Per-step error certificate with survey-sampling variance estimator achieves 0.97 empirical coverage at no accuracy cost on real workloads.

subject: attribution mechanism
statement: The paper shows certificate separates cache-induced from inherent failures (AUC 0.73-0.75) and schedules recomputation better than random or confidence gating.

subject: RRBench framework
statement: The paper introduces open-source RRBench framework for evaluating open-weight LLM agents on data preparation with ground-truth dataset from British cohort study.

subject: benchmark tasks
statement: Framework comprises 20 data preparation tasks including category harmonization and multi-wave merging for creation of 102 variables with automated evaluation routines.

subject: state-of-the-art LLMs
statement: Current state-of-the-art 31-35B parameter models achieved average task completion up to 87.9% on data preparation benchmark.

subject: consumer-grade hardware
statement: The paper shows performance of open-weight LLMs on consumer-grade hardware demonstrates viable path for AI-assisted data preparation in governance-restricted research.

subject: grammatical concept circuits
statement: The paper shows independent code models agree on which grammatical concepts receive dedicated circuits (Spearman ρ = 0.638 Python, 0.673 Rust, p < 10^-7).

subject: circuit layer placement
statement: The paper reports circuit placement is set by model: Qwen processes concepts in late band (L17-19), DeepSeek at L6-7, for both languages.

subject: Rust construct circuitry
statement: The paper shows Rust constructs receive 2-3x more concept-specific circuitry than Python equivalents in both models.

subject: cross-language neuron sharing
statement: The paper reports DeepSeek shares 1.94x more neurons between languages than Qwen across paired constructs.
